title: Crowded, but suspiciously quiet?
caption: Part of Hickson Compact Group 7, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: HCG 7 · constellation Cetus · about 200 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: One spiral galaxy dominates the foreground of this Hubble image, with many more distant galaxies scattered across the background. It belongs to Hickson Compact Group 7, or HCG 7, a tight grouping of three spiral galaxies and one lens-shaped, or lenticular, galaxy.

Crowded groups like this matter because their galaxies evolve differently from those in emptier parts of the Universe. A Hubble study charted three hundred young star clusters and 150 globular clusters in HCG 7, and found that star formation has been fairly steady over time, though high in the central regions.

Other studies hint that the galaxies turned their gas into stars without any help from mergers. But they are using up their gas at a rate that suggests past mergers. Either the group has evolved calmly, or some process not yet understood is at work.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.33 x 3.00 arcminutes) and distance (200 million light years), the frame spans roughly 194,000 × 175,000 light-years. Its light set out about 200 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. A blue filter is coloured blue, a yellow-orange filter green, and a near-infrared filter red.
understand.eye: Part of the data is near-infrared light, invisible to the eye, and the faint background galaxies need Hubble's exposures to appear.

explore: The picture comes from the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, and covers a field 3.3 by 3.0 arcminutes. The group lies about 200 million light-years away in the constellation Cetus.
alt: A spiral galaxy in the foreground with many small, distant galaxies scattered across the background.
